one_line: Nayaka-era engineer-warrior of Gingee, shaping the fort’s water systems and layered defences.

appearance.age_look: late 30s, lean but strong, wiry build
appearance.face: oval face, medium-brown South Indian complexion, sharp nose, neatly kept moustache and short beard line along the jaw, keen focused eyes with a calm but alert default expression
appearance.hair: thick black hair tied back in a short, low knot at the nape, front kept smooth with a small central tilak at the hairline; wrapped in a deep maroon cotton turban band folded flat and low around the head, with one slim tail tucked at the back
appearance.costume: era-accurate South Indian Nayaka noble-officer dress: a long-sleeved, hip-length cream cotton angarkha-style tunic with side tie fastening and a faint woven border; over it a fitted sleeveless dark indigo cotton vest reaching just below the waist, plain but slightly quilted; lower garment is a tightly wrapped off-white cotton veshti/dhoti, pleated in front and tucked for ease of movement, hem reaching to the ankles; a broad brick-red cloth sash is tied firmly around the waist, with a small utilitarian pouch at one side; simple brown leather sandals on the feet; jewellery restrained—thin gold chain with a small round pendant, two plain gold bangles on the right wrist, and small gold stud earrings; a rolled parchment map is tucked at his back under the sash, hinting at planning work
appearance.signature: a straight, medium-length South Indian steel sword (early kattar-type straight blade rather than later ornate forms) with a simple crossguard and dark wooden hilt, carried sheathed at his left hip in a plain brown leather scabbard, plus a small hand-drawn schematic of Gingee’s summit cisterns on palm-leaf panels he occasionally holds when planning

ref_desc: Krishnappa Nayaka appears as a lean, medium-brown South Indian man with a maroon turban, cream angarkha, dark indigo vest, off-white dhoti, brick-red sash, modest gold jewellery and sandals, carrying a plain-hilt steel sword and palm-leaf fort schematics in a cream-indigo-maroon palette.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style character sheet of Krishnappa Nayaka of Gingee: a lean, medium-brown South Indian man in his late thirties with an oval face, sharp nose, neat moustache and jawline beard, and calm, focused eyes. His thick black hair is tied back in a short low knot, wrapped by a flat deep-maroon cotton turban band with a small tail tucked at the back, and he bears a small central tilak at the hairline. He wears a hip-length, long-sleeved cream cotton angarkha-style tunic with side ties and a faint woven border, over which sits a fitted sleeveless dark indigo vest that reaches just below the waist and looks slightly quilted. His lower garment is a tightly wrapped off-white cotton dhoti (veshti), carefully pleated in front and tucked for movement, with the hem down to the ankles, and his feet are in simple brown leather sandals. A broad brick-red cloth sash is firmly tied around his waist, holding a small utilitarian pouch on one side and a rolled parchment map at the back. Jewellery is modest: a thin gold chain with a small round pendant, two plain gold bangles on his right wrist, and small gold stud earrings. At his left hip hangs his signature weapon, a straightforward early South Indian steel sword with a straight blade, simple crossguard and dark wooden hilt, sheathed in a plain brown leather scabbard. Show him also holding or having visible a small bundle of palm-leaf panels bearing schematic drawings of Gingee’s summit cisterns and water systems. Emphasize the cream, dark indigo, maroon, brick red and brown colour palette, and present him in multiple clear poses—front, side and three-quarter—so his face, hair, garments, sash, jewellery, sword and palm-leaf schematics are all easy to redraw consistently.
